stemMd: A town expects a new pedestrian zone to improve shop access for residents with limited mobility. Which finding most seriously qualifies that expectation?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The town has used pedestrian zones elsewhere.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The zone will have a new name.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The scheme removes the only nearby drop-off points, while the nearest accessible public-transport stop is far away.

explanationMd: Access includes reaching the pedestrian area, not merely moving within it. Removing essential arrival points can make access harder for the target group even when vehicle-free streets offer other benefits.

distractorRationale.b: New paving could improve or worsen access; its existence alone does not decide.
distractorRationale.e: Merchandise type is unrelated to reaching the shops.
distractorRationale.c: Naming does not establish mobility barriers.
distractorRationale.a: Past adoption does not establish this scheme's access effects.
